_about: Monster quirks, rolled fresh each time the generator places a monster. Pick a kind by weight, then an entry or a template; fill {table} placeholders from tables, and {pb}, {pb2}, {dc}, {crgold}, {crgold25} from the monster's CR. signature holds one hand-written quirk per classic monster, used signatureChance of the time instead.

templates.text: Among its remains the party finds {object}. {lead}

entries: When it drops to 0 hit points, it explodes in a burst of its own element or nature: each creature within 10 ft takes 2d6 damage of a matching type (DC {dc} Dex save for half).
It can cast misty step once per day as a bonus action.
When it takes damage, it can use its reaction to move half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
It regains hit points equal to {pb} at the start of each of its turns, unless it took radiant or fire damage since its last turn.
Once per day, it can let out a shriek: creatures within 30 ft must make a DC {dc} Wis save or be frightened until the end of their next turn.
It is invisible while it doesn't move.
Its attacks deal an extra 1d6 damage of one type the DM picks (fire, cold, acid, lightning, necrotic or psychic).
Once per day, when it's hit, it can swap places with another creature of its kind within 30 ft, which takes the hit instead.
It can see through magical darkness and illusions within 30 ft.
Once per day, it can make a creature it hits forget the last minute (DC {dc} Int save).
It can climb on any surface, including ceilings, without a check.
Spells that target only it have a 25% chance to fail.
Once per day, it can split into two copies, each with half its current hit points.
It can speak, and it is a terrible liar.
When a creature within 5 ft misses it, it can make one attack against that creature as a reaction.
It leaves difficult terrain behind it (ash, ice, mud or bones) in every space it moves through.
Once per day, it can reflect a spell back at its caster on a successful save.
It can drain mana: a creature it hits loses its lowest-level unspent spell slot or one use of a once-per-rest ability.
It can teleport up to 30 ft between two shadows, once per round.
When it dies, its spirit lingers for one round and makes one last attack.
It can cast one cantrip that fits its nature, using +{pb2} as its spell attack bonus.
Its gaze slows: a creature that starts its turn looking at it must succeed on a DC {dc} Con save or lose its reaction.
It can absorb a nearby corpse as an action to regain 2d8 hit points.
It has a mind link with every creature of its kind within a mile.
It can burrow through dirt and loose stone at half its walking speed.
It can hover and fly at half its walking speed.
Once per day, it can roar to give each ally within 30 ft temporary hit points equal to {pb2}.
When it's reduced below half its hit points, it becomes enraged: it has advantage on attacks and attacks against it have advantage.
Its attacks steal a little life: it regains hit points equal to half the damage of its first hit each turn.
It can mimic any voice it has heard.
It knows when it's being lied to.
It is surrounded by a 10-ft aura of silence.
Once per day, it can turn incorporeal for one round, passing through objects and taking half damage from everything.
It can pull creatures: as an action, each creature within 20 ft makes a DC {dc} Str save or is pulled 10 ft toward it.
It can lay a curse on the creature that kills it: that creature has disadvantage on its next three ability checks.
It can summon 1d4 tiny versions of itself once per day; each has 1 hit point and a weak bite (1d4).
Its blood or ichor is acidic: a creature that hits it with a melee attack takes 1d4 acid damage.
It is immune to being charmed, frightened or put to sleep.
It can see invisible creatures.
Its first attack each combat is a guaranteed critical hit if it was hidden.
It can cast fog cloud once per day, centred on itself.
When it hits a creature, that creature's speed is reduced by 10 ft until the end of its next turn.
It can breathe a 15-ft cone of its element once per day for 3d6 damage (DC {dc} Dex save for half).
It can sense essences: it knows the essences of every essence user it can see, and targets the one it likes best.
Once per day, it can heal another monster within 30 ft for 2d6 + {pb} hit points.
It reforms 24 hours after death unless its remains are burned or blessed.
It is wreathed in a minor ward: the first hit against it each round deals {pb} less damage.
It can make a creature it hits glow with faint light for one minute, removing the benefit of invisibility.
It can cast hold person or hold monster once per day (save DC {dc}), choosing whichever fits.
It can step into any body of water and reappear in another within 1 mile.
Once per day, it can cast shield on itself as a reaction when it is hit by an attack.
When it hits a creature, that creature can't take reactions until the start of its next turn.
Once per day, it can turn invisible as a bonus action until the end of its next turn or until it attacks.
It hunts casters: when a creature within 30 ft casts a spell, it can use its reaction to move up to its speed toward that creature.
Its attacks ignore resistance to their damage type.
Once per day, it can exhale a 20-ft cube of choking spores: each creature inside must succeed on a DC {dc} Con save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn.
When it suffers a critical hit, it can use its reaction to turn it into a normal hit.
Once per day, it can mark a creature it touches; for one hour it always knows the marked creature's direction and distance.
It can devour a monster core or spirit coin within reach as a bonus action, regaining hit points equal to {pb2}.
It grows vengeful: when an ally within 30 ft drops to 0 hit points, it gains advantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.
Once per day, it can slam the ground: each creature within 10 ft must succeed on a DC {dc} Str save or be knocked prone.
It senses mana: it knows the location of any creature within 60 ft that cast a spell or used an essence ability in the last minute.
When it drops to 0 hit points for the first time each day, it drops to 1 hit point instead.
Its attacks prevent healing: a creature it hits can't regain hit points until the start of its next turn.
Once per day, it can fill a 10-ft radius around itself with magical darkness that lasts until the end of its next turn.
It can use its reaction to impose disadvantage on one attack roll made against an ally within 5 ft of it.
Once per day, it can cast dispel magic, adding {pb} to any ability check the spell requires.
When it starts its turn grappled or restrained, it can try to escape with advantage without using an action.
It can move through the spaces of hostile creatures, treating them as difficult terrain.
Once per day, it can create an illusory duplicate of itself; each attack against it has a 50% chance to target the duplicate until the duplicate is hit once.
When it hits a creature with a melee attack, it can push that creature up to 10 ft away.
It has no scent and casts no reflection; it can't be tracked by smell or located by divination magic.
Once per day, it can howl to summon 1d4 local beasts of CR 1/4 or lower, which arrive in 1d4 rounds and fight beside it.
It feeds on fear: it regains {pb} hit points whenever a creature within 30 ft of it becomes frightened.
Once per day, it can harden its outer layer as a bonus action and gain temporary hit points equal to {pb2}.
Its attacks deal double damage to objects and structures.
When it is targeted by a ranged attack, it can use its reaction to add {pb} to its AC against that attack.
Once per day, it can spit sticky resin at a creature within 30 ft: DC {dc} Dex save or be restrained until it uses an action to break free.
It can smell blood: it knows the location of any creature within 60 ft that is below half its hit points.
When it kills a creature, it can immediately move up to half its speed and make one attack.
Once per day, it can release a pulse of disrupted mana: each creature within 15 ft must succeed on a DC {dc} Con save or lose concentration.
It can use an action to see through the eyes of a creature it hit in the last hour, until the start of its next turn.
When it takes lightning damage, its speed doubles until the end of its next turn.
It can't be restrained by nonmagical means, and creatures have disadvantage on checks to grapple it.
Once per day, it can use its reaction when an ally within 60 ft is hit to teleport to an unoccupied space next to that ally.
Once per day, it can flare with blinding light: each creature within 15 ft that sees it makes a DC {dc} Con save or is blinded until the end of its next turn.
It doesn't need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep.
When it takes damage from a spell, it gains resistance to that spell's damage type for one minute.
Once per day, it can pin a creature's shadow within 30 ft: DC {dc} Wis save or the creature's speed is 0 until the end of its next turn.
When it is hit by a melee weapon attack, it can use its reaction to grip the weapon; the attacker must succeed on a DC {dc} Str save or drop it.
It can communicate telepathically with any creature within 60 ft, though only in images and emotions.
Once per day, it can rally its allies: each ally within 30 ft adds 1d4 to attack rolls and saving throws for one minute.
It gains temporary hit points equal to {pb} whenever a creature within 30 ft of it casts a spell of 1st level or higher.
Its hits against a frightened or prone creature are critical hits.
Once per day, it can force a creature within 30 ft to drop whatever it is holding (DC {dc} Wis save).
When it dies, its core cracks open in a burst of mana: each creature within 10 ft gains temporary hit points equal to {pb2}.
It can sink partway into the ground as a bonus action, gaining half cover until it moves.
Once per day, it can cast sanctuary on itself as a bonus action (save DC {dc}).
It can make opportunity attacks against creatures that enter its reach, not only those that leave it.
Once per day, it can make the ground within 20 ft of it erupt with roots, rubble or bone, turning it into difficult terrain for one minute.

It understands every language spoken near it but can't speak.
Its natural weapon attacks count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity.
Its AC can't be lower than 10 + {pb}.

lead: Its owner went missing three weeks ago.
Someone in town will pay well to get it back and ask no questions.
The Adventure Society has a quiet bounty on whoever had it last.
Whoever owned it is still alive and wants it back badly.
It's the second one the party has found this month.
A local fence recognises it and goes pale.
It points to a hidden cache within a day's walk.
The town guard will want to know where the party got it.
A noble family has been searching for it for a generation.
It belonged to a member of a party that vanished in an astral space.
The Magic Society would like to study it, and doesn't like to be refused.
A grieving widow in the market would give anything for it.

It was stolen from a temple vault last season.
It's a forgery, and a good one. Someone is making more.
It matches a description in a very old prophecy.
Its true owner is one of the party's contacts, who swears they never lost it.
It's cursed, mildly, in a way that becomes obvious after a day.
A rival adventuring team is following its trail too.
It leads straight to a smuggler's route through the hills.
It was last seen in the hands of someone who died a year ago.
It's worth almost nothing, but someone will kill for it.
An old soldier in the tavern knows the story behind it.
Whoever lost it left a trail of other strange items behind.
It hums faintly whenever it's near another monster of the same kind.
It is the key to a door the party has already passed.
Its original owner is now a monster too.
A child in the nearest village drew a picture of it last week.
The local lord would rather nobody ever saw it.
It is clearly a message meant for someone in the party.
A Magic Society clerk can trace it to a sealed archive.
It turns up again next week, back on another monster.
Only an essence user with the right essence can read what's written on it.
A merchant caravan due next month was carrying one just like it.
It belonged to an apprentice who ran away from a guild.
The temple will bless the party for returning it.
It's half of a pair, and the other half is somewhere nearby.
Its maker's mark leads to a workshop that burned down.
Rumours in town say whoever holds it can't drown.
A collector in the capital has a standing offer for any like it.
It's the missing piece of a puzzle on a shrine nearby.
It is warm to the touch, and getting warmer.
A street urchin swears they saw the monster take it.
Someone left it here deliberately, as bait.
A dying man asks after it on the road home.
Its inscription names a place not on any map.
It was buried with someone. That grave is now empty.
It belonged to a hero from the last monster surge.
It is listed in the Adventure Society's lost property, with a reward.
Three different people in town claim it is theirs, and none of their stories match.
A Church inquisitor would very much like a word about it.
It was reported stolen from the Adventure Society's evidence room.
It smells faintly of the sea, though the coast is weeks away.
Every dog in town starts howling the moment it passes through the gate.
A pawnbroker offers far too much for it, far too quickly.
It has been mentioned in three unsolved murder reports this year.
It was meant to be delivered to an address that no longer exists.
A bard is already writing a song about it, and getting most of it wrong.
The monster was guarding it, not eating it.
Something else in the area is hunting for it now.
It appears in an old painting hanging in the town hall.
A wealthy widower insists it is a family heirloom and offers a feast for its return.
It was smuggled out of an astral space moments before the space collapsed.
Keeping it overnight gives everyone in the party the same dream.
A Magic Society report describes something identical, and most of that report is redacted.
Its last owner sold it to pay off a gambling debt and bitterly regrets it.
It bears traces of a ritual the Church outlawed decades ago.
A tavern keeper will trade a month of free drinks for it, no questions asked.
It appears on the list of items a missing courier was carrying.
Someone has carefully cleaned it recently, despite where it was found.
A local scholar insists it proves a monster surge is coming.
A pair of masked strangers start following the party once they have it.
It was part of a dowry that never reached the bride.
The priest at the nearest shrine refuses to let it inside.
It is one of a set of seven, and the party now has two.
A retired adventurer recognises it as gear from their old team.
A hermit in the hills will trade a secret trail map for it.
It carries the faint scent of a perfume sold only in the capital.
A goblin tribe considers it sacred and will bargain fiercely for it.
It vanishes from the party's packs at dawn and reappears at dusk.
Tucked beside it is a note with a set of coordinates.
A lost-item notice in the market, written in a child's hand, describes it perfectly.
Selling it would be easy; explaining where it came from would not.
A local alchemist claims it is a rare ingredient and wants every one they can get.
It was stolen from a caravan the party once guarded.
It is covered in tiny claw marks from something much smaller than this monster.
A spirit haunting the old mill keeps asking for it.
The mayor quietly offers silver spirit coins to make it disappear.
It was pawned by a Magic Society member who is now in hiding.
An essence user nearby feels their essences stir whenever it is close.
A note beside it reads 'You're too late,' in fresh ink.
Fresh footprints lead to it and away again, and they aren't the monster's.
A gambler bet his house on someone finding it and is overjoyed the party did.
It is named in a will currently being contested at the courthouse.
It is exactly what a rival adventurer has been bragging about owning.
A travelling merchant insists it's a fake and kindly offers to dispose of it for free.
A hedge witch says it is lucky, as long as nobody ever says thank you near it.
It explains, in a roundabout way, why the monster was here at all.
A team of Adventure Society juniors were sent to retrieve it and never came back.

Bandit.text: Every bandit in this band carries the same tarnished bronze coin, stamped with a crest from a noble house that officially doesn't exist anymore.

Cultist.text: When a cultist drops to 0 hit points, the nearest other cultist within 30 ft regains 1d6 hit points as the dying one's prayer passes to them.

Giant Rat.text: Its teeth are coated in a faint silver residue from gnawing on spirit coins. A dozen teeth can be smelted into 1 iron spirit coin.

Kobold.text: Kobolds here worship a "Sleeping Lord" that is actually an astral space entrance hidden in their warren. They will trade anything to keep it closed.

Stirge.text: After draining blood, a stirge can't be seen through darkvision for 1 minute; the stolen blood masks its body heat.

Skeleton.text: Each skeleton's bones are etched with tally marks; counting them reveals how many times it has been raised. Ones with more than 20 marks have +2 AC.

Zombie.text: A zombie reduced to 0 hit points by non-radiant damage splits into two crawling halves, each with 5 hit points and half its speed.

Giant Frog.text: Its tongue, carefully dried, makes a 15-ft grappling line that sticks to any surface for 1 minute when wet.

Giant Centipede.text: It has 30 legs that can each be shed: once per day when grappled or restrained, it escapes automatically, leaving a writhing leg behind.

Wolf.text: The pack's alpha has a human name collar around its neck, belonging to a missing child from a nearby village.

Blink Dog.text: A blink dog can teleport one willing creature it is touching along with it, and it will do this for anyone who feeds it.

Sprite.text: Sprites keep a ledger of every lie told within their wood. They'll sell a page of it for a song you've never sung before.

Swarm of Bats.text: The swarm flies in formation, spelling out a single word in the air at dusk. The word changes every night and predicts something that will happen tomorrow.

Mud Mephit.text: Its body dries into a lump of clay that heals 1d4 hit points when packed onto a wound, once per creature per day.

Steam Mephit.text: When it dies, the burst of steam it releases makes the area heavily obscured for 1 minute instead of the usual blast.

Smoke Mephit.text: Smoke mephits remember every fire they've been near. Burn something in front of one and it will tell you who last burned something like it.

Constrictor Snake.text: Its scales are so smooth that attacks against it while it's grappling a creature have disadvantage.

Shadow.text: A shadow can step into a creature's own shadow and ride there unseen. While hidden this way it can't be targeted unless the area is magically lit.

Giant Wasp.text: Its stinger holds one dose of paralytic venom: a creature hit with a weapon coated in it must succeed on a DC 11 Con save or be paralyzed for 1 round.

Crocodile.text: It can hold its breath for 6 hours and has advantage on Stealth checks in murky water.

Cockatrice.text: Its feathers are flecked with grey stone. Shedding birds leave trails of pebble-hard plumes that collectors pay 5 gp each for.

Swarm of Insects.text: The swarm is a hive mind that wants to negotiate. Anyone who stands still and lets it crawl over them hears its demand: a new queen, from an astral space.

Worg.text: A worg can speak with any wolf and once per day call 1d4 wolves that arrive in 1d4 rounds.

Satyr.text: Satyrs here run an underground betting ring on gladiator fights in the arena. They know every fixed match.

Dust Mephit.text: Its death burst also covers every creature within 5 ft in dust that outlines them, making invisibility useless for 1 minute.

Ice Mephit.text: Its frozen heart never melts. Dropped into a drink, it keeps it cold for a year and sells for 25 gp.

Magma Mephit.text: It mutters prophecies in a language of hissing stone. Translated, they're bad poetry, but one line in ten is true.

Giant Spider.text: Its webs carry vibration: it knows the location of every creature touching any web within 120 ft.

Specter.text: A specter will stop attacking anyone who speaks its name. The name is carved somewhere in the room where it died.

Ghoul.text: A creature paralyzed by a ghoul hears the voices of the dead it has eaten, and one of them is begging for help.

Imp.text: This imp has been fired by its devil master and is desperately looking for a new contract. It offers terrible advice for free.

Quasit.text: Its invisibility doesn't end when it attacks, but it giggles uncontrollably for a round after, revealing its position.

Animated Armor.text: It still bears the heraldry of a knight who is very much alive and would pay well to have their armour back without questions.

Dire Wolf.text: Its pelt keeps the wearer comfortable in temperatures down to −20 °F and gives advantage on Survival checks to track by scent.

Giant Toad.text: A tiny live creature is always found intact inside its stomach: a lost pet, a fairy, or once, a very annoyed gnome wizard.

Harpy.text: Its luring song mimics the voice of whoever the target trusts most. A target who hears a voice it knows to be dead has advantage on the save.

Brown Bear.text: It has advantage on saves against being frightened and charges: if it moves 20 ft straight toward a target and hits, the target is knocked prone.

Gargoyle.text: Gargoyles on old buildings have watched the streets for centuries. They'll recount any event they saw in exchange for a fresh coat of paint.

Ghast.text: A ghast's stench carries a memory. Anyone who smells it relives the ghast's last living meal, which sometimes reveals where its old treasure is buried.

Gibbering Mouther.text: Its babble includes real words from the creatures it absorbed. Once per encounter, it shouts a true secret about one creature in earshot.

Ochre Jelly.text: A dead jelly leaves behind a perfect acid-etched map of the corridors it crawled through.

Will-o'-Wisp.text: Each wisp is the soul of a guide who led someone to their death. If you follow it and survive, it moves on, leaving a single silver spirit coin.

Nothic.text: The nothic doesn't just learn secrets with its weird insight; it can also trade one, offering a secret about someone else in exchange for one of yours.

Ogre.text: This ogre wears an iron cooking pot as a helmet, giving it +2 AC and making it immune to being stunned.

Grick.text: A grick's beak is mother-of-pearl, and jewellers pay 50 gp each for unbroken ones.

Gelatinous Cube.text: Suspended inside it, half-dissolved, is the gear of the last adventuring party it ate, including one intact magic item.

Mimic.text: This mimic wants to be a real treasure chest. If you open it gently and put a gold coin inside, it won't attack and will follow you as a loyal, if hungry, container.

Merrow.text: A merrow can call the tide: once per day it makes the water within 60 ft rise or fall by 10 ft for 1 minute.

Azer.text: Its beard of flame can be trimmed. Lit embers from it never go out and are prized by smiths, worth 100 gp per lantern.

Sea Hag.text: She's selling back the voices of drowned sailors, sealed in shells. Their families will pay anything to hear them once more.

Basilisk.text: Its gaze turns creatures to glass instead of stone. A petrified creature shatters if it takes 10 or more bludgeoning damage.

Werewolf.text: The werewolf is the village's beloved priest, and he doesn't know. He wakes with blood on his robes and thinks someone is framing him.

Wight.text: A wight's life drain also steals one of the target's memories, chosen by the DM, which returns only when the wight is destroyed.

Hell Hound.text: Its fire gland can be harvested and installed in a forge, letting it reach temperatures hot enough to work adamantine.

Owlbear.text: This owlbear's plumage is snow white, and it is extremely rare. A scholar in town has posted a 500 gp bounty for it alive.

Phase Spider.text: Its bite phases part of the victim into the Ethereal Plane. The target can see invisible and ethereal creatures until its next long rest.

Green Hag.text: She offers to lift a curse from one of the characters, a curse they didn't know they had, which she placed on them when they were children.

Water Weird.text: It is immune to being grappled, and can move through any gap an inch wide as long as water flows through it.

Mummy.text: Its burial wrappings are inscribed with the full map of its tomb, including the traps.

Displacer Beast.text: Its displacement also works on spells: the first spell that targets it each round has a 50% chance of hitting its illusion instead.

Minotaur.text: Minotaurs never forget a path once walked. This one knows every route through the city sewers and wants out of them.

Banshee.text: Its wail doesn't just harm: anyone it drops to 0 hit points sees a vision of how they will truly die, decades from now.

Black Pudding.text: Fire doesn't hurt it. Fire damage makes it split the way slashing and lightning do, so a burning pudding quickly becomes six.

Flameskull.text: A flameskull's flames burn the colour of the wizard's soul who made it, and their name is legible in the fire if you look for 1 minute.

Ghost.text: The ghost is still running its shop. It sells from inventory that no longer exists, and it pays in coin that's still real.

Lamia.text: Her illusions extend to sound and scent. A creature that fails a save against her charm smells home.

Air Elemental.text: When it dies, it leaves a bottled breeze that can fill a ship's sails for 1 day or knock creatures prone in a 15-ft cone once.

Earth Elemental.text: It can't be knocked prone or moved against its will while touching the ground.

Fire Elemental.text: It isn't attacking anyone; it's trying to get home to the Plane of Fire and burning everything in its way to find a door.

Water Elemental.text: Anything it engulfs is also purified: poisons, diseases, and curses end on creatures it releases.

Salamander.text: Its shed skin is fireproof and can be sewn into a cloak that grants resistance to fire for 1 hour per day.

Shambling Mound.text: Its body is full of rare herbs. A healer can harvest enough for 5 potions of healing from it.

Troll.text: The troll has been regenerating so long it has grown back from a single severed hand, and the rest of it is wandering around elsewhere.

Wraith.text: The specters it creates keep the faces and voices of those they once were, and call out to their friends.

Vampire Spawn.text: It is afraid of its own reflection. A creature holding a mirror has advantage on attack rolls against it.

Unicorn.text: The unicorn's horn has been stolen, replaced with a carved bone one. It will grant a wish-like boon to whoever brings it back.

Xorn.text: It eats precious metals, and its droppings are gold nuggets. It leaves 2d10 gp of droppings per day.

Hill Giant.text: It hurls not rocks but livestock, which deal the same damage and leave survivors. A creature hit is also knocked prone.

Gorgon.text: Its petrifying breath leaves creatures as bronze statues instead of stone, worth a great deal to the wrong buyer.

Chimera.text: Each of its three heads wants to go a different direction. Talking one head into an argument with the others gives it disadvantage on attacks for 1 round.

Medusa.text: Her snakes have individual names and personalities, and one of them is secretly helpful, warning intruders with hisses.

Wyvern.text: Its tail venom, properly extracted, is worth 200 gp to assassins and alchemists.

Invisible Stalker.text: Whoever summoned it died before it finished its task. It's still hunting a target who has since become someone important.

Drider.text: It can speak through any spider within a mile, and has been listening to the town for years.

Stone Giant.text: Its skin is covered in carved runes that tell its clan's history. A scholar could read them and learn the location of an ancient vault.

Young Black Dragon.text: Its acid breath also dissolves magic: the first nonmagical armour or shield it hits is destroyed.

Oni.text: The oni is the town's most popular merchant. Its prices are fair, its goods are real, and every so often a customer just disappears.

Hydra.text: Each new head that grows back is a different colour and breathes a different element.

Young Green Dragon.text: It has taken a village hostage, but it doesn't want gold. It wants a philosopher to argue with, and it will let one villager go for each argument it loses.

Frost Giant.text: Its axe is made of ice that never melts, keeping a cutting edge forever and dealing extra cold damage.

Spirit Naga.text: When it dies, its spirit returns in 1d6 days unless its body is buried at a temple.

Chain Devil.text: Its chains can bind a creature's soul as well as its body; a grappled creature can't be healed.

Bone Devil.text: It runs a legitimate law practice in the city's back streets, handling property contracts. Every contract has a clause no one has read.

Clay Golem.text: It was sculpted to look like its creator, who has since died, and it still waits for their orders.

Cloud Giant.text: The cloud giant hosts a feast every full moon in a castle in the sky. Invitations are mailed by eagle, and declining is considered an insult.

Fire Giant.text: Its forge-born armour is still hot when it dies; a smith can rework it into a single suit of +1 plate.

Young Blue Dragon.text: Its lightning breath leaves the ground electrified: any creature that starts its turn in the line takes 2d6 lightning damage.

Treant.text: The treant is slowly dying of a rot in its roots that only a rare herb from an astral space can cure.

Deva.text: A deva can see through any lie as it's spoken. Creatures can't deceive it with Deception checks.

Stone Golem.text: Its core is a single gem, the source of its animation, worth 1,000 gp, or more to a golem-maker.

Young Red Dragon.text: Its scales are oddly patterned, and anyone who studies them can see a map of a mountain range with one peak marked.

Aboleth.text: It remembers the world before the gods, and it can prove that one of them is not what they claim to be.

Behir.text: It can store a lightning strike in its body. During a storm, its breath recharges on a 4–6 instead of 5–6.

Djinni.text: The djinni is bound to grant three wishes, but it's been stuck in a lamp so long that its wishes have gone sour and literal.

Efreeti.text: Its brass bottle is still around, and anything sealed in it is preserved forever, unaging.

Horned Devil.text: Its wings beat so hard that creatures within 10 ft when it takes off must succeed on a DC 15 Str save or be knocked prone.

Remorhaz.text: Its back plates radiate heat for a year after it dies, enough to keep a mountain lodge warm through any winter.

Erinyes.text: She's hunting an oathbreaker, and one of the characters fits the description of someone who broke a very old promise.

Vampire.text: It can drink from a creature's shadow instead of its blood, draining strength without leaving a mark.

Rakshasa.text: In a mirror, it appears as whoever the viewer trusts most. This is how it chose its current disguise.

Storm Giant.text: The storm giant is a prophet, and it's been dreaming of the characters for years.

Ice Devil.text: The ground around it is always frozen; creatures within 10 ft have their speed halved.

Adult Black Dragon.text: Its hoard includes a dozen sunken ships' logbooks, each marking the location of other treasure.

Mummy Lord.text: It can command the sand: once per day it creates a 30-ft-radius sandstorm that blinds every creature but it.

Purple Worm.text: Inside its stomach is an entire village, still alive, which has built homes from the bones of other things it swallowed.

Iron Golem.text: It is magnetized. A metal weapon that hits it sticks fast, and pulling it free takes an action and a DC 15 Strength check.

Planetar.text: The planetar has lost its faith and is asking mortals what they believe in, and why.

Marilith.text: Each of her six arms wields a different weapon, and she can parry six attacks per round.

Adult Red Dragon.text: It wears a crown, and claims to be the rightful heir of a kingdom it burned. The surviving nobles are oddly quiet about it.

Dragon Turtle.text: An entire coral reef grows on its shell, full of pearls, and fishermen ride on it unaware it's alive.

Androsphinx.text: The sphinx's riddle has no answer. Anyone who realizes this and says so passes.

Balor.text: When it dies, its explosion also tears a small rift to the Abyss that lasts 1 hour unless sealed.

Pit Fiend.text: It holds the contract for the soul of the realm's ruler, and is willing to trade it.

Ancient White Dragon.text: It can freeze time within its lair once per day, giving it an extra turn at initiative count 20.

Lich.text: Its phylactery is hidden in plain sight as an everyday object in the city, being passed around as currency.

Solar.text: The solar has been sent to kill one of the characters, and it's very, very sorry about it.

Ancient Black Dragon.text: Its lair actions spread across a whole swamp; within 6 miles, every creature with a reflection is being watched.

Kraken.text: It is so old that islands have formed on its back, and they are populated.

Ancient Gold Dragon.text: It's been living as a human scholar for three centuries and has a family who doesn't know.

Ancient Red Dragon.text: Its hoard is protected by a curse: each coin taken increases a bounty on the taker by 1 gp until it reaches the hoard's full value.

Tarrasque.text: It has been asleep for a thousand years, and something is trying to wake it. The characters are the only ones who can hear its heartbeat.
